question: True or false: most near-Earth asteroids big enough to destroy a city, 140 m or more across, have already been found?
answer: False. Surveys have found nearly all the kilometre-wide ones that could cause global damage, but well under half of the estimated 25,000 of 140 m or more. Smaller, darker rocks are hard to spot against the sky, which is why NASA is building a dedicated infrared telescope to hunt them.
move: A list of known dangers is not a list of all dangers.
ask: Which risk in my plans is missing from my list just because nobody has spotted it yet?
trap: True, since agencies seem to track every rock that makes the news.
source: NASA Center for Near Earth Object Studies
